expression: {f: function(n) if n = 0 then true else sort([1, 2], function(a, b) f(n - 1))[1] = 1, r: f(80)}.r
why: The function that `sort` and `list replace` call is invoked like any function (DMN 1.6 Table 64; §10.3.4.9, Table 81: precedes is a "boolean function of 2 arguments defined on every pair of list elements"; Table 76: the match of `list replace` is a function), and an invocation counts toward the limit of 200 nested function calls, an implementation limit that stops the evaluation (docs/CONTRACT.md section 2). A recursion through the callback is 3 calls deep per level (the function, the built-in and the callback), so 80 levels exceed the limit; the previous release did not count the callback, so 2 calls per level stayed under it.

error.message: function calls are nested too deeply (more than 200 levels, e.g. runaway recursion); evaluation stopped
